searchText: following up on this. if i were to want to write an EIP is there like a guide or something or an implementation- which eth impl should i do this against? can i pick? can i do revm or hevm or another rust one? would i need to do test vectors? Gm i'd just pick another EIP and use that as a template if you want to implement in Geth or another execution client, that would help demonstrate the complexity of the EIP's change test vectors aren't exactly required but the more you do the more convincing your argument for "why this change and why now" is this being said, are there concrete, compelling use cases for this particular hash fn as a precompile? this is just my one take but i'm not seeing enough so far to justify this addition (point being, i'd work on having wide buy-in on the motivation before even doing any of the engineering work) https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/eip-template.md Makes sense. Is this the right place to try and get that buy-in? thanks <@301186049323958275> I put a defense of why I think this should be added on ethmagicians but I’m not sure how to get people to engage hehe The hardest part of the Ethereum development process is getting people to engage.

test vectors aren't exactly required but the more you do the more convincing your argument for "why this change and why now" is
